reason: Both reach the right conclusion: the element is the likely cause, the regulator or board is possible, and an engineer should test it. Neither asks for the full model number. Conversation 1 is more efficient and has fewer technical slips, and it clearly explains why dismantling the glass is unsafe before recommending an engineer. Conversation 2 wrongly describes ceramic hobs as having 'solid plates' and suggests peering under the glass with the hob unplugged. It also says the control logic is working and tells the customer an engineer will 'replace the faulty part' before anything has been tested, which is slightly overconfident.
